main_body: Half-timbered house with a large hipped tile roof over cream plaster walls, plus a front porch with a gable and a door
top_band: The roof slope runs from about row 2 to row 43 in mid-brown (#804530) tile courses with dark joints (#49252c). It reads as a large foreshortened top surface sitting above the light plaster walls.
evidence: The hipped roof shows its top slopes (ridge, hips, chimney cap). Below it a dark eave row at about row 43-45 separates it from the lighter plaster front wall, which is rows 44-75 plus the porch below. The porch has its own gable with a triangular pediment. The doors and windows are framed in dark brown, so they read as inset. The roof/wall step is clear (L 84 to L 182), so this is a correct 3/4 structure.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours against 185 and 66 in the references, and 3 colours per tile against 18 and 11. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral (#16161a), against 7-9% in the references, so the outline is a near-black sticker line instead of a tinted dark material tone. Flat-fill coverage is 17% against 0%. The plaster walls are large flat cream areas with no speckle. The roof tiles are a regular two-tone pattern with no per-tile highlights or scallops. The result is far shallower than the references.
